Hi Maya / Procurement Team —

Attached is our redline of the Order Form (Proposed_Order_Form_v2_redline.pdf) plus a short commentary from Commercial. High level asks:

- Confirm you can accept a split-invoicing approach: 40% on signature (invoice triggers), 40% on activation (first production month), 20% on usage settlement at month 6. This is reflected in Section 2 of the redline.
- Net terms: your standard is Net45 — we can accommodate Net45 for invoices after the first milestone, but need Net30 for the signature invoice due to internal cashflow gating. Seeking a waiver or a commercial credit if Net45 is required across the board.
- Taxes: please confirm whether Acme will withhold any local taxes on Redwood invoices. If withholding applies, we need a gross-up and supporting tax residency evidence (we've attached Tax_Residency_Cert_Acme.pdf for your AP/Tax team to review).
- Minimum commit cadence: redline proposes a quarterly true-up to reconcile committed vs. actual spend; please confirm whether that cadence works for your finance team or if you need monthly true-ups.

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow (Fri) 10:00–11:30 PT to resolve tax and invoice-splitting? If you prefer, send your commercial counter with any non-starter items and we can loop Legal.

Attachments: Proposed_Order_Form_v2_redline.pdf, Tax_Residency_Cert_Acme.pdf

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer

Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Thanks for the redline and the clear list. A few quick items from Procurement/Finance after a first pass:

1) Net terms: Acme standard is Net45 across the board. We can discuss exceptions but need a commercial justification for Net30 on signature. Will your team consider a small onboarding discount in place of Net30?

2) Invoice split: We prefer a 50/30/20 split (signature/activation/settlement) to align with our ERP — would Redwood accept shifting to 50% upfront?

3) Withholding tax: Acme may be required to withhold local taxes depending on jurisdiction. We need Redwood to confirm whether Redwood will accept withholding OR provide a gross-up. If Redwood cannot gross-up, we will need the WHT language in the Order Form that allows Acme to deduct and provide certificates.

4) Minimum commit true-up: Monthly true-ups are preferable for finance accuracy. Quarterly would add complexity for our accounting.

Can Kimberly (cc'd) and your Finance lead help surface whether Redwood can accept 50/30/20 and monthly true-ups? Also attaching our procurement PO template for reference (not attached in this thread).

Best,
Maya Patel
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
maya.patel@acme-corp.com

Maya / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick feedback. A few Legal/Commercial notes after reviewing the proposed 50/30/20 split and the withholding question:

- Invoice split: Redwood can accept the 50/30/20 profile provided there is clear definition in the Order Form for the activation milestone (what constitutes activation) to avoid disputes. We would propose replacing the ambiguous "activation" with a short acceptance checklist (Annex A) tied to the first production workload.

- Net terms: Net45 is standard for Acme but Redwood's collections team prefers Net30 for signature invoices only. If Acme requires Net45 across all invoices, Redwood requests a 5% onboarding fee credit to offset the extended terms on the signature invoice (we've outlined this option in Commercial_Commentary.docx).

- Withholding tax: Redwood is prepared to accept statutory withholding. However, Redwood will require: (i) Acme to provide official withholding certificates within 60 days of payment; (ii) a gross-up for any amount that cannot be credited against Redwood's tax liability. If Acme cannot provide certificates, Redwood will invoice the gross amount and seek relief via netting in the following quarter.

- Monthly true-ups: Commercially acceptable, but note operational overhead. If moving to monthly true-ups, we propose a simplified reconciliation template (we can share a CSV sample) and a soft cap on adjustments under $1,000 to avoid churn.

I can take the attached redline and produce a counter-redline with those edits (i.e., Annex A activation definition, monthly true-up table, and withholding certificate timing), unless Acme prefers to propose alternate language.

Attaching: Commercial_Commentary.docx.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
